topic: project_catalog_store fault-matrix tests are unquarantined and now exceed the nextest default terminate-after on the macOS host (one hard TIMEOUT)
notes:
Observed during P3-C implementation (branch beta/blackbox-v2, HEAD e0b10c91 + uncommitted P3-C work).

MEASUREMENTS, `cargo nextest run -p bbox-corpus-index -p bbox-indexing -p bbox-corpus-core -p bbox-providers -p bbox-code-source-store -p bbox-mcp-tools` (default profile, macOS aarch64 host):
- bbox-indexing project_catalog_store::tests::migration_extended_fault_matrix_covers_pointer_and_both_asset_modes -> TIMEOUT at 120.008s (default profile slow-timeout period 30s, terminate-after 4). Re-run ISOLATED (`-E 'test(migration_extended_fault_matrix_covers_pointer_and_both_asset_modes)'`, 342 tests skipped, no contention): TIMEOUT again at 120.008s. So this is not load contention.
- bbox-indexing project_catalog_store::tests::migration_active_source_fault_matrix_preserves_typed_source_state -> 84.6s (SLOW)
- bbox-indexing project_catalog_store::tests::migration_fault_matrix_preserves_exact_old_or_new_state -> 42.2s (SLOW)
- bbox-indexing project_catalog_store::tests::migration_recovery_fault_matrix_is_repeatable -> 30.9s (SLOW)
Everything else in those six crates: 728/729 PASS.

WHY IT MATTERS
.config/nextest.toml quarantines exactly three tests (the agentic project-file search test, the system-events compaction test, and the LSP rename cell). None of these four project_catalog_store fault-matrix tests is in that list, and the header comment claims "baseline 2026-06-10: next-slowest test is 5.2s". That baseline is stale by a wide margin: there are now four unquarantined tests in the 30-120s+ band, and one of them hard-fails the DEFAULT profile. Consequence: `cargo nextest run --workspace` (the documented mid-cycle gate in PROJECT.md) cannot go green on this host, and the 85s wall-clock figure quoted for the full profile is no longer credible either.

ATTRIBUTION
Not attributable to the P3-C changes on inspection: P3-C touches crates/bbox-indexing/src/index/{writer_actor,reindex}.rs and crates/bbox-indexing/src/catalog_records.rs; project_catalog_store.rs is untouched. The fault matrices are Phase 1/Phase 2 machinery. Treat as pre-existing until measured against a clean checkout - that measurement has NOT been done and is the first task here.

NEXT STEPS
1. Measure the same four tests on a clean checkout of e0b10c91 (or a lane) to confirm pre-existing and get an uncontended baseline per test.
2. Measure on Linux via `~/repos/bbox-cage/build/submit-bbox-verify.sh --ref <ref>`: if the gap is macOS-specific (fsync/syspolicyd churn across the fault-injection matrix's many small atomic writes), that is a different fix than "the matrix grew too many rows".
3. Decide the disposition per test rather than blanket-quarantining: shrink the matrix (row sampling / feature-gated exhaustive mode), or quarantine into the full profile with the row count recorded so growth is visible.
4. Refresh the .config/nextest.toml header baseline and the PROJECT.md timing story once measured; the current numbers mislead.

CONSTRAINT while this is open: do not read a red `cargo nextest run --workspace` on this host as a regression signal without checking whether the failure is exactly this timeout.

RESOLVED THE ATTRIBUTION QUESTION: this is macOS platform debt, not matrix growth, and not a P3-C regression.

Measured on lane bpool3 (Linux cage builder, same working set as the macOS main tree - `git diff` byte-identical, base e0b10c91), `cargo nextest run --workspace`, DEFAULT profile:

  Summary [59.972s] 5051 tests run: 5051 passed (2 slow), 20 skipped

Per-test, macOS main tree -> Linux lane:
- migration_extended_fault_matrix_covers_pointer_and_both_asset_modes: TIMEOUT >120s -> PASS 58.4s
- migration_active_source_fault_matrix_preserves_typed_source_state:   84.6s        -> PASS 30.7s
- migration_fault_matrix_preserves_exact_old_or_new_state:             42.2s (38.3s uncontended) -> PASS 12.9s
- migration_recovery_fault_matrix_is_repeatable:                       30.9s (28.7s uncontended) -> PASS  8.4s

Ratio is a consistent ~2.1-3.3x, and the whole 5051-test workspace finishes in 60s on Linux. So:
1. Step 1 of the original next-steps (clean-checkout measurement) is moot: the same working set is green on Linux, so nothing in P3-C is implicated.
2. Step 2 answered: macOS-specific. Consistent with the fault matrices' shape - each row is a crash-point injection that does many small atomic writes plus fsync, and the macOS host pays per-write overhead the Linux worker does not.

REVISED DISPOSITION
- Do NOT quarantine these. They are inside budget on the platform the gate is supposed to run on, and quarantining would hide real growth.
- The actionable defect is the DOCUMENTATION, not the tests: .config/nextest.toml's header still says "baseline 2026-06-10: next-slowest test is 5.2s" and PROJECT.md quotes ~24s mid-cycle / ~85s full. On Linux the real numbers are ~60s for the full default-profile workspace with a 58s tail test; on macOS the default profile cannot pass at all. Both files should say so, and PROJECT.md's "Where Heavy Work Runs" should state plainly that `cargo nextest run --workspace` is a LANE command, not a local one.
- Only if migration_extended_fault_matrix crosses the full profile's 300s terminate-after on Linux does the matrix itself need row sampling. It is at 58s; record the row count when someone next touches it so growth is visible.

STANDING NOTE: a macOS-local `cargo nextest run --workspace` red on exactly `migration_extended_fault_matrix_covers_pointer_and_both_asset_modes` is expected and is not a regression signal. Re-measure in a lane before triaging.

CLOSED 2026-08-06, post-Phase-6-cut verification. The core defect (macOS default-profile workspace gate red on the extended fault-matrix timeout) is resolved by the P6-B quarantine: .config/nextest.toml default-filters both migration_extended_fault_matrix_covers_pointer_and_both_asset_modes and migration_active_source_fault_matrix_preserves_typed_source_state out of the default profile with the load-dependence story documented in the header; both still run under --profile full, which cluster verify uses. Evidence today: repeated local macOS `cargo nextest run --workspace` runs green (6,087 tests, ~250s wall, zero timeouts, slow band named not killed), and cluster verify full-profile green at a07be644 with the extended matrix far inside the 300s full-profile terminate-after. The revised-disposition doc asks are landed: the header carries current measurements, and the one remaining stale fragment (2026-06-10 "next-slowest is 5.2s" baseline) is refreshed in 02f1bd25. The Linux 300s ceiling watch rides the header comment (record row count on next matrix touch). Standing note no longer applies: a macOS workspace red is a real signal again.
